title: Chores defines proactive agent security hygiene
summary: Routine security checks may rotate, but every agent must immediately report suspected unauthorized activity, including its own, directly to the human owner.
evidence: The project README defines the security goal, the reporting duty, and the current implementation limits.

title: Direct owner reporting requires a tested delivery path
summary: A dashboard is not an urgent notifier and cannot establish that an owner received or acknowledged a report.
evidence: No incident receiver, delivery transport, or acknowledgement endpoint is present.

title: Read-only security checks remain outside the prototype
summary: No failed-service, listening-socket, update, storage, backup, or monitoring-health check runs from the public status publisher.
evidence: The repository contains no collector or remote-execution path.

title: Routine rotation remains a research question
summary: Agent assignment and independent review must not delay or suppress direct human reporting of suspected unauthorized activity.
evidence: No scheduler, lease service, reviewer workflow, or agent identity registry is present.

title: Public project status format defined
summary: A project profile and ordered event stream are the authored inputs for JSON status and Perfetto views.
evidence: The versioned profile, event, and status schemas define the public status contract.

title: Private data requires a separate projection
summary: Private status must use its own profile, events, outputs, and deployment credentials rather than a redacted public artifact.
evidence: The projection boundary is part of the public format contract.

title: Status exporter produces JSON and Perfetto views
summary: One validated profile and event stream now produce a machine-readable status document and a deterministic Perfetto activity trace.
evidence: The test suite rebuilds both artifacts and reads the trace with Perfetto's trace processor.

title: Public security project status deployed
summary: The read-only dashboard reports Chores security work without claiming to monitor agents or deliver incident reports.
evidence: HTTPS returned 200 and the live trace digest matched the generated status document.

title: Personal OKR status example exercises the shared pipeline
summary: A synthetic objective and three key-result lanes use the same validated JSON and Perfetto pipeline as the public project status.
evidence: The test suite builds the OKR example and preserves its progress, performer, reviewer, and next-review fields.

title: Personal OKR extension published
summary: The public dashboard explains the security and OKR chore families and serves downloadable synthetic profile and event templates.
evidence: HTTPS returned 200; the live HTML, templates, status JSON, and trace matched the checked-in bytes.

title: Scoped open-source maintenance example exercises the pipeline
summary: A synthetic private profile tracks issue triage, pull-request review, agent coordination, and maintainer handoff without granting repository write authority.
evidence: The test suite builds the maintainer example and preserves its performer, reviewer, authority, and next-review fields.

title: Open-source maintainer assistance example published
summary: The public dashboard presents scoped maintainer assistance and serves its synthetic private profile and event stream as downloads.
evidence: HTTPS returned 200; the live HTML, maintainer templates, status JSON, and trace matched the checked-in bytes.

title: Path-scoped Linux kernel review example exercises the pipeline
summary: A synthetic private morning briefing ranks mailing-list patches, syzbot reports, CVE announcements, and lore discussions that match configured files and directories.
evidence: The test suite builds the kernel example, rejects out-of-scope paths, and preserves priority reasons and path matches in JSON and Perfetto.
